events.title: Hong Kong Stock Market May Extend Monday's Gains
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has alternated between positive and negative finishes through the last five trading days since the end of the three-day slide in which it had given up almost 600 points or 2.5 percent. The Hang Seng now sits just above the 23,830-point plateau and it's tipped to open in the green again on Tuesday.

events.title: Overbought Taiwan Shares Nonetheless Called Higher Again
events.description: The Taiwan stock market has moved higher in four straight sessions, climbing more than 2,050 points or 4.4 percent along the way. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 49,700-point plateau and it may see mild upside again on Tuesday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market May Crack Resistance At 5,700 Points
events.description: The Singapore stock market on Monday snapped the four-day losing streak in which it had slumped almost 100 points or 1.8 percent. The Straits Times Index now sits just above the 5,660-point plateau and it's expected to open to the upside again on Tuesday.

events.title: Malaysia Bourse May Add To Its Winnings On Tuesday
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has finished higher in two straight sessions, although it has advanced less than two points or 0.1 percent in that span. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just above the 1,630-point plateau and it may pick up steam on Tuesday.

events.title: Japan Stock Market May See Additional Support
events.description: The Japan stock market rebounded on Monday, one session after ending the two-day winning streak in which it had surged almost 3,500 points or 5.6 percent. The Nikkei 225 now sits just beneath the 69,950-point plateau and it may extend its gains on Tuesday.

events.title: Win Streak May Continue For South Korea Shares
events.description: Ahead of Monday's market holiday for National Foundation Day, the South Korea stock market had climbed higher in two straight sessions, advancing more than 160 points or 2.3 percent along the way. The KOSPI now sits just above the 7,000-point plateau and it may add to its winnings again on Tuesday.

events.title: Australia Consumer Confidence Data Due On Tuesday
events.description: Australia will on Tuesday see October results for the consumer confidence index from Westpac Bank, highlighting a light day for Asia-Pacific economic activity. In September, the index slumped 5.2 percent on month.

events.title: TSX Comes Off Early Lows, Up Marginally
events.description: The Canadian equity benchmark S&P/TSX Composite Index was marginally Monday afternoon, recovering gradually from an early setback. Elevated bond yields and persisting worries about geopolitical tensions limited market's upside.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Modestly Higher
events.description: Save for a minute or two early on in the day, the Switzerland stock market's benchmark index SMI stayed positive right through the trading session on Monday thanks to strong and sustained buying at several counters.

events.title: European Stocks Close Mixed As PMI Data, Political Concerns Shape Trading
events.description: European equities posted mixed results Monday, with Germany and UK gaining ground while France declined to a 7-month low amid fiscal and political uncertainty. The Stoxx 600 rose 0.36%, reflecting investor caution over regional PMI data and bond yields.

events.title: U.S. Services Index Indicates Modestly Slower Growth In September
events.description: A report released by the Institute for Supply Management on Monday showed a modest slowdown in the pace of growth in U.S. service sector activity in the month of September. The ISM said its services PMI dipped to 54.9 in September after rising to 55.4 in August, although a reading above 50 still indicates growth. Economists had expected the index to edge down to 55.0.

events.title: Eurozone Private Sector Growth At 41-Month High
events.description: The euro area private sector expanded at the fastest pace in nearly three-and-a-half years in September amid rising demand and employment, final purchasing managers' survey data from S&P Global showed Monday. The composite output index posted 53.1 in September, in line with flash estimate, and above August's 52.0.

events.title: Bay Street Likely To Open On Mixed Note
events.description: Canadian shares look headed for a somewhat mixed start Monday morning, tracking crude oil and precious metals prices. Additionally, PMI data and corporate news are expected to provide some direction to the market.
